source_user: Advanced cluster case NVIDIA Dynamo-122: Design an evaluation of NVIDIA Dynamo for disaggregated inference orchestration. Variant 122 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate frontend routing, prefill workers, decode workers, KV movement, transport overhead, scheduling policy, queueing, model compatibility, observability, and failover behavior. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assumptions and scope: pin and verify the deployed NVIDIA Dynamo release, model/tokenizer, software/driver/CUDA versions, GPU/NIC/RDMA topology, and configuration; declare context and output-length distributions, request mix, concurrency, offered load, batching, cache warmth, placement, tenant policy, correctness, and deadline targets. Do not infer release-specific behavior without documentation or an observed trace. Falsifiable hypothesis for this variant: under matched workload, model quality, and offered load, disaggregated Dynamo disaggregated inference orchestration changes a predeclared primary metric (p95 TTFT, p99 end-to-end latency, or completed requests/s) by a predeclared margin while p99 ITL, timeout/error rate, output correctness, isolation, and cost remain within predeclared limits. Use least-privilege, read-only inspection first to verify readiness, frontend/admission, prefill, decode, KV lifecycle and movement, transport/RDMA, scheduling, queueing, compatibility, observability, and failover, correlated request IDs, and compatibility before changing anything. Compare against a current-production or non-disaggregated baseline with identical model, traffic, batching, placement constraints, and quality checks; report p50/p95/p99 latency, TTFT, ITL, throughput, queue time, utilization, bytes, error/timeout rate, and cost with units, confidence intervals, and strata. Attribute effects with synchronized traces and ablations rather than aggregate latency alone. Run only a bounded canary or fault injection with redacted outputs and a tested return to the known-good route. Roll back immediately if any predeclared SLO, correctness, compatibility, authorization/isolation, error/timeout, or data-integrity gate regresses; retain traces, counters, and configuration diffs. Evidence required before claiming improvement: pinned inventories, raw synchronized traces, repeated matched trials, ablations, negative results, fault-injection/recovery outcomes, and rollback artifacts.

source_user: Advanced cluster case multi-node NCCL-1: A multi-node NCCL job hangs only at larger world sizes. Produce a falsifiable diagnosis and rollback plan. Variant 1 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: test rank mapping, interface selection, topology, NIC affinity, rendezvous, firewall and ports, timeout logs, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assumptions and scope: pin NCCL, CUDA, driver, framework, launcher, and network-fabric versions; record node/GPU/rank mapping, NIC and NUMA affinity, selected interfaces, routing, MTU, ports/firewall policy, rendezvous endpoint, topology, and job shape. Treat the hang as a synchronization or communication failure, not proof of a specific cause. Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 1: the larger-world-size hang is caused by a rank-to-rank path or communicator-formation defect (for example inconsistent interface/topology selection, unreachable rendezvous/port, NIC affinity mismatch, or a fabric fault) that appears when a particular rank pair or edge is introduced. Reproduce with a minimal collective and a binary-search sequence of world sizes, holding message size and software constant; compare a known-good smaller world, alternate rank mappings, and a control-plane-only rendezvous. Capture per-rank NCCL debug timestamps, selected transport/interface, communicator state, timeout location, launcher logs, packet/connection counters, link errors, and GPU/NIC telemetry with units. Correlate the first missing rank pair and test connectivity/ports read-only before changing configuration. Change one variable at a time in an isolated canary, with bounded timeouts and no production traffic. Roll back to the last known-good world size, rank mapping, interface and NCCL settings if the control test regresses, if a link or node becomes unhealthy, or if retries risk duplicate work; preserve logs and configuration diffs. Evidence required: a reproducible smallest failing world size, matched reduced-world baseline, rank-pair/path correlation, fabric and timeout counters, and a successful rerun after the narrowly scoped remediation. Do not claim root cause until these observations agree; if they do not, classify it as unresolved and escalate with artifacts.
risks: NCCL and fabric behavior is version and topology dependent; verify rather than assume transport selection.
A larger world size changes rank pairs, routes, resource pressure, and timeout exposure, so aggregate success/failure alone is insufficient.
Diagnostics or configuration changes can disrupt jobs; use read-only checks, isolated canaries, bounded timeouts, and a known-good rollback.
evidence_required: Pinned NCCL/CUDA/driver/framework/launcher and fabric inventory.
Per-rank NCCL logs with timestamps, transport/interface and communicator state.
Rank mapping, topology, NIC/NUMA affinity, rendezvous/port checks, and network/GPU counters.
Reproduction matrix, reduced-world controls, minimal collective, remediation rerun, and rollback artifacts.
